falsificationAssay.question: Per the unbuilt-affects note (sections 1 and 3), condition 2 of the hope proposal requires: 'no member of H(G, π) is reachable without further play — the outcome cell is at ⊥, not at t' for a genuine position/chronicle-prefix π. The note names as the falsification risk: 'if the corpus's chronicles are always finite and fully enumerable at read time, then condition 2 never holds... which would make hope vacuous in this substrate.'
falsificationAssay.finding: CONFIRMED RISK: every chronicle in this substrate is fully enumerated (maximal) at read time; there is no position/prefix type and no undetermined (⊥) outcome cell anywhere in genre.mts or the Chronicle type it consumes. Condition 2 as stated cannot be satisfied by the current substrate.
citations: src/structuring/concurrent-game/with-symmetry/ludicizing/chronicle.mts, lines 1-22: 'A design is the union of its chronicles... The validity judgment realizes the four chronicle conditions (Ch1)-(Ch4): unit-step child chain, polarity alternation, ramification respect, and MAXIMALITY (end at a Daimon or at an empty ramification).' The Chronicle type (lines 45-48: `interface Chronicle { readonly kind: "game.chronicle"; readonly actions: readonly Action[]; }`) carries no partiality/openness field; maximality is a construction-time condition, not something the type or its constructor (chronicle(), lines 50-55) can leave unsettled.

src/genre.mts, line 87: `export function genre(chronicles: readonly Chronicle[]): Genre` takes an already-complete, already-enumerated array of maximal chronicles as its whole input — there is no position/prefix parameter, and none of genre()'s internals (resolving = chronicles.filter(resolves).length, line 89; surrenders, line 90; exemplar(), lines 55-59) read anything but a finished array.

src/genre.mts, lines 21-24: `resolves = (c) => { const last = c.actions[c.actions.length - 1]; return last !== undefined && last.variety !== "daimon"; }` inspects the LAST action of an already-terminated chronicle — there is no branch of this logic that can return anything but a determined true/false (i.e. t or f on the truth order); no ⊥ (undetermined/held-open) value is ever produced or consulted.
falsificationAssay.conclusion: As built, apps/playing's Chronicle is Girard's maximal play (root-to-leaf path), and genre()/resolves() operate purely over such already-maximal chronicles supplied wholesale. Nothing in the substrate models a live 'position' (a chronicle prefix still being played) or a bottom-valued (⊥) outcome cell. This is the exact vacuity risk the unbuilt-affects note names in section 3's falsification path, not a hypothetical: derive-continuation-reading.mjs cannot satisfy condition 2 by reading genre.mts/affect.mts alone; it needs a new position/prefix carrier over an unclosed (non-maximal) event structure — the same open obligation the note (section 3, citing the 2026-08-22 obsmetrological unclosed-arena note) and section 9 direction 1 both name — before hope (as distinct from a settled reachability query) can be represented at all. This is the first fact the continuation reader's brief needs.
